source.title: Ridge interpolators in correlated factor regression models -- exact risk analysis

record.file_problem: none; full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The study analyzes excess prediction risk as overparameterization changes in factor regression models, a different model family from deep networks, and tests double-descent behavior with theoretical analysis and simulations.
record.gate_note: The study reports double-descent behavior for FRM risk and the effect of optimally tuned ridge regularization, so these bear on V4 and V6. Other versions are not tested. Cited findings about neural networks and other papers are not recorded as results. Figure 1 and Figure 2 include curves, but the text does not provide their plotted point values.
record.test_reason: The study derives exact asymptotic excess-risk formulas, with simulations, for GLS and ridge in factor regression models. It shows double descent in the overparameterization ratio and that optimally tuned ridge smooths it. That is a new model class carrying results on V4 and V6, so T3 rather than T2.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that FRM GLS excess risk shows double descent and that optimally tuned ridge can completely smooth it. They add that ridge's benefit is marginal above ratio 5 and nil above 10. They also stress that untuned interpolation performs about as well as tuned ridge, and that consistency is achievable under proper scaling.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses Random Duality Theory to analyze classical ridge, GLS, and LS estimators in correlated factor regression models, rather than the original deep-network settings.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported ridge-smoothing effect depends on the overparameterization ratio: it is limited above 5 and virtually nonexistent above 10. The simulations also examine correlated and uncorrelated setups.
record.problems: The numerical curves are mostly presented in figures without pointwise values in the text. The claims concern factor regression models and do not directly test deep networks. Multiple-peak behavior and the proposed noise mechanism are not evaluated directly.

untested.parts: Not stated explicitly. Simulations fix n and vary m, so the ratio axis is partly a sample axis, but the text never reports that more data raises risk.
Model classes other than linear factor regression.
Whether label noise or variance drives the peak, and whether multiple peaks occur.

missing.what: Limiting GLS risk as α→0 of about 0.14963 (cl=4, κ=1/2). Risk vanishes as κ→0 (consistency).
Near-threshold underparameterized point α⁻¹=0.7: LS risk 0.9751/0.9756 vs optimal ridge 0.3764/0.3759.

record.verdict_notes: This is a purely theoretical linear-model study, so the verdicts concern V4/V6 only for factor regression. The r3 limits_scope label was dropped: weak ridge gains far from the peak do not contradict peak removal.

versions.untested_parts: Deep-network test error as model size changes.
Changing training sample size near an interpolation threshold.
The tested model class is factor regression, not all model classes; the study does not establish a universal curve across classes.
A single effective-complexity measure predicting peak locations across size, epochs, and sample count.
Whether label noise or variance drives the peak, whether peaks split into multiple descents, and whether optimally tuned regularization removes peaks in all settings.
Whether counting complexity by an effective parameter count turns the second descent into an ordinary U-shaped curve.

rows.subject: FRM GLS interpolator
rows.operation_detail: Simulate excess prediction risk across overparameterization ratios

conditions.value: correlated FRM; q = 0.5, qv = 0, qe = 0.3, qL = 0.3, σe² = 0.01

rows.baseline: Null risk is plotted; no numeric baseline stated for the curve
rows.value: The text describes the risk curve as U-shaped and says it turns upward only at strong overparameterization, on the order of a few tens.
rows.note: The study reports agreement between theoretical curves and simulated points but gives no pointwise curve values in the text.
rows.check: In the correlated setup, risk falls after interpolation but turns upward again at ratios of a few tens. That is a U-shape, not a sustained second descent. The factor SNR is built to decay as 50·α with the ratio (eq. 182), which confounds the upturn.

source_check.correct: The simulation uses σ² = 0.2, rather than σ = 0.2. The text states a limiting null risk of 2 for q = 0.5; the finite-dimensional null risk decreases as the overparameterization ratio increases. The risk turns upward at ratios of a few tens as factor SNR = 50α declines.
source_check.locator_found: Section 5.1, Figure 1 setup; equations (179)–(182) and surrounding paragraphs.
source_check.problem: The noise variance is recorded as a standard deviation, and the baseline omits the explicitly stated limiting value.

source_check.correct: Figure 2 uses cL = 4n/k = 4/(ακ), with constant cl = 4; cL is not fixed at 4. The text describes double descent and monotonic behavior under proper scaling. Section 5.2.1 gives limiting GLS risk approximately 0.14963.
